title: Jefferies’ Chris Wood Sees ‘Massive Capital Destruction’ in AI
key_facts: Chris Wood is Jefferies' global head of equity strategy.
His base case is that US hyperscalers will not earn returns sufficient to justify their AI investments, leading to significant capital destruction (said in a 17 Sep interview).
The investment is increasingly financed by debt rather than cash.
He said 'the moment credit markets effectively withdraw funding, the entire AI trade could unravel'.
Competition from cheaper Chinese models could pressure prices providers can charge.
AI capital spending was still accelerating in September; he gave no timetable for a downturn.
Chip companies could keep benefiting while investors and lenders keep financing AI spending.
quote_evidence: My base case remains that they will not generate returns sufficient to justify those investments. Ultimately there will be significant capital destruction.
The key difference now is that this investment is increasingly being financed through debt rather than cash.
The moment credit markets effectively withdraw funding, the entire AI trade could unravel.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known strategist says debt-funded AI spending may not pay off; no date is given.
event_date: 17 Sep 2026 (interview per TokenPost); Bloomberg headline 9 Oct 2026
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (403). Text read at TokenPost, which dates the interview 17 Sep; whether Bloomberg's 9 Oct story is a new interview is not known. Older view re-dated.
